alloy.preparation: Ni80Cr20 wire sample, reported as 80% Ni:20% Cr (Discussion, PDF p. 10). The general method uses as-received wire washed in distilled water and methanol, with 0.25 mm wire formed into a 25 mm diameter loop attached to the holder of Fig. 1b and immersed halfway to expose 0.32 cm^2 (PDF p. 2).

test_solution.preparation: Prepared using reagent-grade chemicals and distilled water, with pH adjusted using H2SO4 or NaOH as required. Nitrogen was bubbled through the solution for 24 hours to reduce oxygen to a negligible value; the three-electrode glass cell was purged with nitrogen during each experiment (Experimental method, PDF p. 2).

test_method.procedure_description: Potentiodynamic polarization using the wire-loop electrode system (Fig. 1b) in a conventional three-electrode glass cell. A Princeton Applied Research Model 273 potentiostat/galvanostat with Model 342 Softcorr software controlled potential and measured current. Before each measurement, the sample was introduced into the electrolyte at -800 mV (SCE) and held for 5 minutes to ensure a reproducible surface; the polarization scan rate was 60 mV min^-1. All reported potentials refer to saturated calomel. The scan end potential and electrolyte temperature are not specified (Experimental method, PDF pp. 2-3). Figure 9 condition: Ni80Cr20, 1.0 M NaCl, pH 3.

test_method.pitting_criterion: Definite pitting potential from the polarization plot where evident; otherwise the potential corresponding to an anodic current density of 10 μA cm^-2 was plotted. The paper does not identify which individual Fe/Ni/Mo markers use the current criterion (Discussion, PDF p. 10).

experiments.result_note: The experimental-method text states that presented results average at least three identical experiments; no individual replicates or unreported uncertainty are inferred. The Discussion says definite pitting potentials were used where evident; otherwise the potential at 10 μA cm−2 anodic current was plotted. It does not identify affected markers; this point is not asserted to be a proxy or an unequivocal pitting threshold. The material is identified by its elemental wire designation; no numerical purity or composition assay is reported, so its element amount is null rather than an inferred 100%.
